auth.description: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2 access token sent as a bearer; short-lived, minted outside flux (delegated sign-in or application client-credentials), and refreshed by the host rather than by generated Flux
auth.name: microsoft_graph.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: An OAuth2 access token for Microsoft Graph, minted through an Entra ID app registration with the delegated or application permissions the enabled operations need (Mail.Read and Mail.Send for mail, MailboxSettings.Read for Outlook settings, Calendars.ReadWrite for calendar, Files.ReadWrite for files). flux is handed an already-minted token; it does not perform the sign-in or client-credentials grant itself
config.label: Microsoft Graph access token
config.name: access_token

description: Microsoft Graph: read and reply to Outlook mail, inspect Outlook settings, read and create Calendar events, and read and rename OneDrive files

operations.description: Get one Outlook message by id: subject, sender, recipients, timestamps and the body — HTML by default. This is personal correspondence; treat the sender, recipients and body as personal data

params.description: The message's id, an opaque string Graph itself reports on a prior list or get — never invented. Excludes `/`, `?`, `#` and `&`, the four characters that could change the shape of the request; the emitted Flux does not enforce this, so it is a contract a model reads rather than a validator
params.name: message_id

body.description: `{contentType, content}` — HTML by default. Send `Prefer: outlook.body-content-type="text"` to get plain text instead, which this connector does not do: no header parameter is declared, so every body here arrives as HTML

bodyPreview.description: A plain-text extract of the body, truncated. Personal correspondence — never an example value here

conversationId.description: Groups messages in the same thread

from.description: `{emailAddress: {name, address}}` — the sender. Personal data, never an example value here

id.description: The message's id — what this operation takes

internetMessageId.description: The RFC 2822 `Message-ID`, distinct from Graph's own `id`

parentFolderId.description: The mail folder this message currently lives in

toRecipients.description: Each `{emailAddress: {name, address}}`. Personal data, never an example value here

webLink.description: Opens the message in Outlook on the web. Requires the viewer's own sign-in session; does not itself carry a credential

operations.description: Reply to a message. Graph resolves the recipients automatically — the original message's `replyTo` if it specifies one, otherwise its `from` — and this operation cannot override, widen or add to that audience (C-56 excludes the `message` override Graph's own reply action accepts). Delivered within seconds and cannot be recalled

params.description: The id of the message being replied to
params.name: message_id

params.description: Text to prepend above the quoted original message. May be an empty string — Graph accepts that — but the field itself must always be sent
params.name: comment

operations.description: List the top-level mail folders in the signed-in user's mailbox — Inbox, Drafts, Sent Items, and any custom top-level folders. Does not descend into subfolders. Graph's default page size here is 10; this connector cannot follow `@odata.nextLink` (an absolute URL, not a constructible cursor), so a mailbox with more than ten top-level folders is reported incompletely

value.description: First page only — see this operation's own description. Each folder is `{id, displayName, parentFolderId, childFolderCount, unreadItemCount, totalItemCount, isHidden}`

displayName.description: e.g. `Inbox`, `Drafts`, `Sent Items` — localized to the mailbox's own language

operations.description: Get one calendar event: its subject, start and end, organizer, attendee list and cancellation state. Returned in UTC unless a `Prefer: outlook.timezone` header is sent, which this connector does not do

params.description: The event's id, as Calendar's own listings report it
params.name: event_id

attendees.description: Each `{type, status: {response, time}, emailAddress: {name, address}}`, where `status.response` is `none`, `accepted`, `declined` or `tentativelyAccepted`. Personal data throughout, never an example value here

body.description: `{contentType, content}` — HTML by default, the same convention as the mail body above

iCalUId.description: Identifies this event across calendars, distinct from Graph's own `id`

id.description: The event's id — what this operation takes

isAllDay.description: When true, `start`/`end` represent midnight in the stated time zone rather than a real time of day

isCancelled.description: **A cancelled event is still returned by this operation**, with `isCancelled: true`. Check this before treating the event as live

location.description: `{displayName, ...}` — free text, not a structured address

organizer.description: `{emailAddress: {name, address}}` — who owns the event. Personal data, never an example value here

seriesMasterId.description: Present when this event is one instance of a recurring series

start.description: `{dateTime, timeZone}`. By default `dateTime` is UTC; a `Prefer: outlook.timezone` header (not sent here) would change it

subject.description: Absent-titled events render as an empty string, not a missing member

webLink.description: Opens the event in Outlook on the web. Requires the viewer's own sign-in session; does not itself carry a credential

operations.description: Create a single-instance event on the signed-in user's default calendar. No attendees can be declared yet (C-56), so nobody is invited and nobody is notified — the event appears only on the calendar it was created on

params.description: The event's title, as it appears on the calendar grid
params.name: subject

params.description: When the event starts, as a local date-time with no UTC designator — `2026-01-30T09:00:00` — interpreted in `start_time_zone`
params.name: start_date_time

params.description: The IANA or Windows time zone name `start_date_time` is expressed in, e.g. `UTC` or `Pacific Standard Time`
params.name: start_time_zone

params.description: When the event ends, in the same local, no-designator form as `start_date_time`. Must be after it; Graph rejects an end that precedes its start
params.name: end_date_time

params.description: The time zone `end_date_time` is expressed in
params.name: end_time_zone

attendees.description: ABSENT on every event this operation creates: no attendee can be declared yet (C-56), so nobody was invited and nobody was notified

id.description: The new event's id — the only handle on it, and what `microsoft_graph-calendar-event-get` reads back

organizer.description: The token's own account. Personal data, never an example value here

subject.description: Echoes the title that was sent

webLink.description: Opens the event in Outlook on the web. Requires the viewer's own sign-in session; does not itself carry a credential

operations.description: Get the signed-in user's own default calendar: its name, colour and sharing/editing permissions. This is the calendar, not its events — use microsoft_graph-calendar-event-get for one of those. Takes no argument: `/me/calendar` always resolves to the token's own default calendar

allowedOnlineMeetingProviders.description: Which online-meeting providers can be attached to events on this calendar, e.g. `teamsForBusiness`

hexColor.description: A custom hex colour when `color` is set to a custom value; empty string otherwise

id.description: The calendar's own id, distinct from any event's id

isRemovable.description: `false` for the default calendar — it cannot be deleted

name.description: The calendar's display name, e.g. `Calendar` for the default one

owner.description: `{name, address}` — the mailbox this calendar belongs to. Personal data, never an example value here

operations.description: Get one OneDrive item's metadata by id: its name, size and where it lives. This never returns file content — downloading needs the separate /content endpoint, which returns a binary body and is not shipped by this connector

params.description: The item's id, an opaque string OneDrive itself reports on a prior listing or get — never invented
params.name: item_id

cTag.description: Changes when the item's content changes; `eTag` also changes on a metadata-only edit

createdBy.description: `{user: {id, displayName}}` — whoever created the item. Personal data, never an example value here

file.description: Present when this item is a file rather than a folder — `{mimeType, hashes}`

folder.description: Present when this item is a folder rather than a file — `{childCount}`. `file` and `folder` never both appear on the same item

id.description: The item's id — what this operation takes

lastModifiedBy.description: Same shape as `createdBy`. Personal data, never an example value here

parentReference.description: `{driveId, id, path}` — the folder this item lives in

webUrl.description: Opens the item in a browser. Requires the viewer's own sign-in session; does not itself carry a credential

operations.description: Rename a OneDrive item: sets its name and changes nothing else. Does not move it — moving is a PATCH to the separate parentReference field, which this operation deliberately does not declare (C-56)

params.description: The item to rename
params.name: item_id

params.description: The item's new name
params.name: name

file.description: Present when this item is a file rather than a folder

folder.description: Present when this item is a folder rather than a file

name.description: The name **after** the update. Compare it against what was sent

parentReference.description: Unchanged by this call — a rename never moves the item

webUrl.description: Opens the item in a browser. Requires the viewer's own sign-in session; does not itself carry a credential

categories.description: The categories associated with the item

lastModifiedDateTime.description: The Timestamp type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z

attachments.description: The fileAttachment and itemAttachment attachments for the message.

isInline.description: true if the attachment is an inline attachment; otherwise, false.

lastModifiedDateTime.description: The Timestamp type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z

size.description: The length of the attachment in bytes.

bccRecipients.description: The Bcc: recipients for the message.

address.description: The email address of the person or entity.

name.description: The display name of the person or entity.

bodyPreview.description: The first 255 characters of the message body. It is in text format.

name.description: The display name of the person or entity.

conversationId.description: The ID of the conversation the email belongs to.

conversationIndex.description: Indicates the position of the message within the conversation.

extensions.description: The collection of open extensions defined for the message. Nullable.

id.description: The unique identifier for an entity. Read-only.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in a combined date and time representation ({date}T{time}; for example, 2017-08-29T04:00:00.0000000).

timeZone.description: Represents a time zone, for example, 'Pacific Standard Time'. See below for more possible values.

completedDateTime.description: The date and time that the follow-up was finished.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in a combined date and time representation ({date}T{time}; for example, 2017-08-29T04:00:00.0000000).

timeZone.description: Represents a time zone, for example, 'Pacific Standard Time'. See below for more possible values.

dueDateTime.description: The date and time that the follow-up is to be finished. Note: To set the due date, you must also specify the startDateTime; otherwise, you get a 400 Bad Request response.

flagStatus.description: The status for follow-up for an item. Possible values are notFlagged, complete, and flagged.

dateTime.description: A single point of time in a combined date and time representation ({date}T{time}; for example, 2017-08-29T04:00:00.0000000).

timeZone.description: Represents a time zone, for example, 'Pacific Standard Time'. See below for more possible values.

startDateTime.description: The date and time that the follow-up is to begin.

flag.description: Indicates the status, start date, due date, or completion date for the message.

address.description: The email address of the person or entity.

name.description: The display name of the person or entity.

from.description: The owner of the mailbox from which the message is sent. In most cases, this value is the same as the sender property, except for sharing or delegation scenarios. The value must correspond to the actual mailbox used. Find out more about setting the from and sender properties of a message.

hasAttachments.description: Indicates whether the message has attachments. This property doesn't include inline attachments, so if a message contains only inline attachments, this property is false. To verify the existence of inline attachments, parse the body property to look for a src attribute, such as .

importance.description: The importance of the message. The possible values are: low, normal, and high.

inferenceClassification.description: The classification of the message for the user, based on inferred relevance or importance, or on an explicit override. The possible values are: focused or other.

internetMessageHeaders.description: A collection of message headers defined by RFC5322. The set includes message headers indicating the network path taken by a message from the sender to the recipient. It can also contain custom message headers that hold app data for the message.  Requires $select to retrieve. Read-only.

name.description: Represents the key in a key-value pair.

value.description: The value in a key-value pair.

internetMessageId.description: The message ID in the format specified by RFC2822.

isDeliveryReceiptRequested.description: Indicates whether a read receipt is requested for the message.

isDraft.description: Indicates whether the message is a draft. A message is a draft if it hasn't been sent yet.

isRead.description: Indicates whether the message has been read.

isReadReceiptRequested.description: Indicates whether a read receipt is requested for the message.

multiValueExtendedProperties.description: The collection of multi-value extended properties defined for the message. Nullable.

id.description: The unique identifier for an entity. Read-only.

parentFolderId.description: The unique identifier for the message's parent mailFolder.

receivedDateTime.description: The date and time the message was received.  The date and time information uses ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z.

replyTo.description: The email addresses to use when replying.

address.description: The email address of the person or entity.

name.description: The display name of the person or entity.

name.description: The display name of the person or entity.

sender.description: The account that is used to generate the message. In most cases, this value is the same as the from property. You can set this property to a different value when sending a message from a shared mailbox, for a shared calendar, or as a delegate. In any case, the value must correspond to the actual mailbox used. Find out more about setting the from and sender properties of a message.

sentDateTime.description: The date and time the message was sent.  The date and time information uses ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z.

singleValueExtendedProperties.description: The collection of single-value extended properties defined for the message. Nullable.

id.description: The unique identifier for an entity. Read-only.

toRecipients.description: The To: recipients for the message.

address.description: The email address of the person or entity.

name.description: The display name of the person or entity.

contentType.description: The type of the content. Possible values are text and html.

uniqueBody.description: The part of the body of the message that is unique to the current message. uniqueBody is not returned by default but can be retrieved for a given message by use of the ?$select=uniqueBody query. It can be in HTML or text format.

webLink.description: The URL to open the message in Outlook on the web.You can append an ispopout argument to the end of the URL to change how the message is displayed. If ispopout is not present or if it is set to 1, then the message is shown in a popout window. If ispopout is set to 0, the browser shows the message in the Outlook on the web review pane.The message opens in the browser if you are signed in to your mailbox via Outlook on the web. You are prompted to sign in if you are not already signed in with the browser.This URL cannot be accessed from within an iFrame.NOTE: When using this URL to access a message from a mailbox with delegate permissions, both the signed-in user and the target mailbox must be in the same database region. For example, an error is returned when a user with a mailbox in the EUR (Europe) region attempts to access messages from a mailbox in the NAM (North America) region.
